The `ClassUtils.getShortClassName` method takes a `Class<?>` parameter and returns the short class name. If the parameter is `null`, it returns `StringUtils.EMPTY`, which is an empty string `""`.

In the failing test case, the assertion is expecting the short class name of `String[]` to be `"String[]"`. However, the current bug report indicates that a semicolon is added to the end of the class name for arrays, causing the assertion to fail.

Based on the code snippet of `getShortClassName(Class<?> cls)` method, it simply returns the short class name of the given class name without any special handling for arrays. This suggests that the issue lies in how arrays are handled in the method.

To fix this issue, we need to modify the `getShortClassName` method to handle arrays correctly so that it does not append a semicolon at the end of array class names.

Next, I will suggest a location to fix this issue.
```java
org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(java.lang.Class<?>)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug.
